title: The Rare bird on the marsh
subtitle: 动物世界 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）
meta: 主题语境：动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）　|　核心词汇：rare　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rare 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the craftsman wrote of ① a rare bird on the marsh in the ledger, and everybody in the workshop said at once that it was ② rarer than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the craftsman, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the rare ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the rarest bird on the marsh anybody in the workshop had ever seen, or so the ledger for August 1958 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too rare to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the apprentice who had come to help; the rare ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a rare gift for languages, and said that no apprentice in his right mind would call it ⑥ as rare as the gift for languages they had once had in the old workshop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was rare or not, and he said so.

By 1971 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the ledger. What the line asked for was ⑦ something rare, and nothing besides. The apprentice from the next workshop called the whole plan ⑧ quite rare; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the ledger kept the names of the rare ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1974, without complaint, she wrote of another rare bird on the marsh in the same ledger, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ rarer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The rarest gift for languages in the whole workshop, she said in 1976, was the one she could never quite name; the rare ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 罕见（前置定语 a rare bird on the marsh：1964 年匠人在工料簿里记下的那件罕见的稀有鸟类）
B. adj. 罕见／稀有（比较级 rarer than：文中两处，一处比湿地上的稀有鸟类，一处比预想）
C. adj. 罕见／稀有（最高级 the rarest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 罕见（表语 too rare to do：母亲觉得它太罕见，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 稀有（前置定语 a rare gift for languages：叔叔把整件事称作一桩稀有的语言天赋）
F. adj. 稀有（同级比较 as rare as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩罕见的语言天赋相比）
G. adj. 稀有（后置定语 something rare：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 稀有（受程度副词修饰 quite rare：那位学徒的评价）

items.q: a rare bird on the marsh
the rarest bird on the marsh anybody
The rarest gift for languages in

answers.why: rare 意为“罕见”，1964 年匠人在工料簿里记下的是“一件罕见的稀有鸟类”，此处作前置定语 a rare bird on the marsh。
rare 意为“罕见”，此处用比较级 rarer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
rare 意为“罕见”，工料簿上 八月 那行字说它是工坊里最罕见的一件，故用最高级 the rarest bird on the marsh。
rare 意为“罕见”，母亲认为这件东西“太罕见了，谁也用不上”，too rare to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
rare 意为“稀有”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩稀有的语言天赋”，此处作前置定语 a rare gift for languages。
rare 意为“稀有”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩罕见的语言天赋一样稀有”，同级比较用 as rare as。
rare 意为“稀有”，工料簿上那半行字要的是“稀有的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something rare。
rare 意为“稀有”，邻工坊来的那位学徒认为这套计划“相当稀有”，quite 修饰原级 rare。
rare 意为“稀有”，1974 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要稀有”，故用比较级 rarer than。
rare 意为“稀有”，母亲 1976 年说的是“整个工坊里最稀有的那一桩”，故用最高级 the rarest gift for languages。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1964 年，匠人在工料簿里记下了一件罕见的稀有鸟类。（a rare bird on the marsh）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更罕见。（rarer than …）
母亲觉得它太罕见，谁也用不上。（too rare to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩稀有的语言天赋。（a rare gift for languages）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩罕见的语言天赋一样稀有。（as rare as …）
到了 1971 年，工料簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件稀有的东西。（something rare）
answers: In 1964 the craftsman wrote of a rare bird on the marsh in the ledger.
Everybody said it was rarer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too rare to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a rare gift for languages.
He said nobody would call it as rare as the gift for languages they had once had.
By 1971 the ledger asked for nothing but something rare.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 rare 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1964 the craftsman wrote of a rare bird on the marsh in the ledger, and nobody forgot it.
It was the rarest bird on the marsh in the workshop, or so the ledger says.
My mother thought it too rare to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a rare gift for languages, and nobody argued with him.
The apprentice from the next workshop called the plan quite rare, and everybody laughed.
The rare ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
